1_Learning_Objective.Title: 🎯 The "Why Are We Learning This?" (Learning Objective)
1_Learning_Objective.Content: This chapter teaches your child the polite words we use to greet people at different times of the day (Good morning, Good night) and basic manners (Hello, Please, Thank you). It builds social skills and confidence in talking to others!

2_The_Hook.Title: 🪝 The Hook (How to start the conversation)
2_The_Hook.Content: When you wake them up or open the curtains, excitedly ask: **'If the Sun could talk, what's the first thing it would say to us when it comes up in the morning?'** Wait for their answer, then say, **'It would say Good Morning! Did you know words are like magic keys that make people smile? Let's learn a few magic words today.'**

Mini_Lessons.What_To_Say: Tell your child: 'When the sun is waking up, we say Good Morning. When the sun goes to sleep and the moon comes out, we say Good Night.'
Mini_Lessons.Home_Example: Use a flashlight in a dark room. Shine it on the ceiling and say 'The sun is up! What do we say?' (Good Morning!). Turn it off and say 'The sun is gone! What do we say?' (Good Night!).

Mini_Lessons.What_To_Say: Tell your child: 'When we see our friends, we wave and say Hello! When it is time to go home, we wave and say Goodbye!'
Mini_Lessons.Home_Example: Have your child walk out of the room and walk back in. Practice waving a big 'Hello!' and then having them walk out while saying 'Goodbye!'

Mini_Lessons.What_To_Say: Tell your child: 'When we want something, we use the magic word Please. When someone gives us something nice, we say Thank You.'
Mini_Lessons.Home_Example: During snack time, hand them a biscuit only when they say 'Please'. Then prompt them to say 'Thank you' once they receive it.

4_Common_Stumbling_Blocks.Title: 🚧 Common Stumbling Blocks (What to watch out for)
4_Common_Stumbling_Blocks.Content:
Kids often confuse **'Good Evening'** and **'Good Night'**. 
*   **How to clarify:** Explain that 'Good Evening' is for playtime when it's just getting dark, but we are still awake. 'Good Night' means we are going into our bed to sleep.

Questions.Question: What do we say to Grandma when we wake up?
If I give you your favorite toy, what is the magic word you should say?
It is dark outside, but we are eating dinner and not sleeping yet. Do we say Good Evening or Good Night?

Activities.Name: 1. The Sun and Moon Game
Activities.Description: Hold a yellow plate (Sun) and a white pillow (Moon). Pop the plate up and have them shout 'Good Morning!' Swap to the pillow and have them pretend to snore and say 'Good Night!'

Activities.Name: 2. Teddy Bear Tea Party
Activities.Description: Sit down with their soft toys. Have the toys 'visit' each other. Practice making the toys say 'Hello', 'Please pass the tea', and 'Goodbye' to each other.

Activities.Name: 3. The Greeting Race
Activities.Description: Run to different rooms in the house. In the bedroom, pretend to sleep (Good Night). In the kitchen, pretend to eat breakfast (Good Morning). At the front door, pretend to leave (Goodbye).

Activities.Name: 4. The Magic Word Pass
Activities.Description: Roll a ball back and forth. The person rolling must say 'Please take this' and the person catching must say 'Thank you!' Keep it going as fast as you can.
